answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: a continuous, prescribed chain of modular squarings is sequential because each square depends on the prior result. An attacker can copy credentials to create apparent clones, but cannot divide one chain among GPUs or make its steps simultaneous; every clone therefore pays the same measured delay. Whether representing a voyage, island, or pearl, each identity must earn its own proof, making Sybil expansion physically expensive.
